title: Research: C4 root-lift obstruction for four outputs (no kappa)
body:
## Result

This package gives an exact scoped minimum of four calls for the target `diag([g^2],[g^2],[g^2],[g^2])` in `F2[C4]` on four registers. An augmentation-filtration argument excludes every word of length at most three in the alphabet `D_N([g^s]) = I + ([g^s]+[e])N`, `s in {1,2,3}`, with rank-one idempotents `N in M4(F2)`. Four coordinate calls attain the target.

The proposed three-call root-lift had a favorable abstract rank screen (rank budget 9 against target rank 8); the exact coefficient argument closes this specific candidate. A three-register pilot also checks all 7,056 ordered two-call words and finds no witness for three `[g^2]` outputs.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/bit-c4-root-lift-seedca46bc/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-c4-root-lift-seedca46bc --check-only
```

Both commands pass locally on CPython 3.14.7. The registered package runner requests Python 3.12, which is unavailable locally; the pull request package workflow will run its declared replay on the hosted runner.

## Scope and provenance

The changed model is a four-register finite cyclic torsion address group. It differs from the pinned torsion-free rational-frame three-register result. It has no rational-frame conversion, physical supplier admission, or new `kappa` claim. The selected result remains complex-bound at `kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000`.

The task seed is `ca46bc53e5dd5aaf9ff33154b9e78646`, `bit-mechanisms / bit-new-register-model`, priority revision 4. Exact research base: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`; selected-record SHA-256: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. Source, predecessor, selected review, source manifest and certificate pins are recorded in `SOURCES.json`.

The final overlap refresh completed with 429 open PRs and 867 Discussion/comment records, complete pagination and no warnings. The exact query found no remote matches. The scoped claim is in [Discussion #2185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2185).

Prepared by Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No independent human review is claimed.
